newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends weak after volatile session.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends weak after volatile session.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter futures settled weak after see-sawing throughout the session amid conflicting ideas about the extent of freeze damage to the crop, traders said.

Traders cautioned that it will be some time before a clear picture develops of how much wheat was damaged. During that time, they said, the market will probably remain edgy as private estimates of crop damage emerge.
"Part of the reason we broke is that the market felt top heavy. Also, overnight trade was not as high as people expected, which was disappointing," a trader said.
"Plus, maybe when it came to damage estimates, people may have thought that the numbers touted yesterday were on the high side," the trader said.
Private estimates have reportedly pegged the amount of wheat lost anywhere from 60 million to 300 million bushels.
KCBT wheat stabilized early after faltering at the opening amid profit taking and talk that damage to the crop may not be as severe as originally thought, traders said.
KCBT wheat settled 13 to 1-1/4 cents lower, with May wheat down six cents at $4.70-1/2 per bushel and July down 2-1/4 cents at $4.47-3/4.
Traders said Wolcott Lincoln sold four million July bushels.
Prudential Securities was a key player, buying two million July, 1.2 million September and selling 1.8 million July. Prudential also bear-spread 1.3 million July/May.
